notes:
OCRelay 1.1.24

NEW: US DVT LOWER EXTREMITY

• "Lower Extremity" is now the first type under US DVT in the Study picker, for the bilateral lower extremity venous duplex.
• For each leg, each vein's circled + or − becomes its line in the report (common femoral, femoral proximal/mid/distal, popliteal, calf veins). A "+" alone becomes "Thrombus present.", and the review panel asks you to choose occlusive or nonocclusive.
• Abnormal/flat phasic flow rewrites the Flow line, and absent augmentation rewrites the Augmentation line. A negative worksheet already matches the report, so nothing is changed.
• A red alert names the side and vein of any thrombus, because the impression still reads negative. If the worksheet marks only one leg, it warns that the other leg's section keeps its normal sentences.
